'''''Salix repens''''', the '''creeping willow''', is a small, shrubby species of [[willow]] in the family [[Salicaceae]], growing up to 1.5{{nbsp}}metres in height. Found amongst sand dunes and heathlands, it is a [[polymorphism (biology)|polymorphic]] species, with a wide range of variants. In the UK, at least, these range from small, prostrate, hairless plants at one end of the spectrum to taller, erect or ascending silky-leaved shrubs at the other.<ref name=BSBI>{{cite book |last1=Meikle |first1=R.D. |title=Willows and Poplars of Great Britain and Ireland. BSBI Handbook No.4 |date=1984 |publisher=Botanical Society of the British Isles |location=London |isbn=978-0901158079 |pages=140–145 |ref=BSBI}}</ref> This wide variation in form has resulted in numerous [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonyms]].<ref name = PlantList>{{Cite web |url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-5003472 |title=''Salix repens'' L. — The Plant List |website=www.theplantlist.org |language=en |access-date=2017-12-09}}</ref>

==Distribution==
The plant has a Eurosiberian Boreo-temperate range, and is widely distributed around the coasts of western and northern Europe.<ref name = brc>{{Cite web |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=plant/salix-repens |title=''Salix repens'' |publisher=Biological Records Center |website=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |language=en |access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cwbHHvlXIoEC&pg=PA225 |title=Plant Life of the Quaternary Cold Stages: Evidence from the British Isles |last=West |first=R. G. |date=2000-04-13 |page=225 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=9780521593977 |language=en}}</ref>

In the UK, the prostrate forms (ssp. ''argentea'' and ssp. ''repens'') are characteristically found on [[sand dune]]s, growing close to the water table in [[dune slack]]s, as well as in coastal heaths and [[acid grassland]], as well as being found further inland on [[heath]]s and [[moorland]]. The erect form (var. ''fusca'') occurs in [[fen]]s. The species becomes more confined to moist or wet habitats in the southern and eastern parts of its UK range, and has been recorded from sea level up to {{convert|855|m|ft|0}} (in [[Perthshire|East Perthshire]]).<ref name = brc/>

==Ecology==
Dunes containing ''Salix repens'' are recognised as being of ecological importance by the [[EU Habitats Directive]]. Over 132 [[Natura 2000]] sites are designated for this habitat type. As the water table lowers within the slack, these ''Salix''-dominated habitats (termed Salicion arenariae) may develop either into mesophilous (neither wet nor dry), or [[Xerophile|xerophilous]] (dry) communities. The former may contain species such as ''[[Pyrola rotundifolia]]'', ''[[Viola canina]]'' and ''[[Monotropa hypopitys]]''; the latter containing ''[[Carlina vulgaris]]'' and ''[[Thalictrum minus]]''.<ref name=eunis>{{Cite web |url=http://eunis.eea.europa.eu/habitats/10044 |title=EUNIS -Factsheet for Dunes with ''Salix repens'' ssp ''argentea'' (Salicion arenariae) |website=eunis.eea.europa.eu |access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://jncc.defra.gov.uk/protectedsites/sacselection/habitat.asp?FeatureIntCode=H2170 |title=SAC selection - 2170 Dunes with ''Salix repens'' ssp. ''argentea'' (Salicion arenariae) |website=jncc.defra.gov.uk |language=en |access-date=2017-12-11}}</ref>

''Salix repens'' provides shelter to other species of plant and animal. Its soft, fluffy seed hairs provide nesting material for [[songbird]]s, whilst in autumn there is often a rich assemblage of unusual [[fungus]] species growing in its vicinity.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://species.nbnatlas.org/species/NBNSYS0000003877#overview |title=Salix repens : Creeping Willow {{!}} NBN Atlas {{!}} NBN Atlas |last=Atlas |first=NBN |website=species.nbnatlas.org |language=en-AU |access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref>

Should the dune slack that the plant inhabits become inundated by an advancing dune, it is able to adapt and change its growth form from erect to prostrate. Losing its erect habit, the plant is able to creep horizontally along the front of the advancing dune and survive the changing conditions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=STOMPS |first=THEO. J. |title=The Dunes of Lake Michigan |date=1915 |jstor=43477467 |journal=The Plant World |volume=18 |issue=8 |pages=205–216}}</ref>

Studies have shown that [[mycorrhizal]] fungal associations may assist ''Salix repens'' in expanding the ecological niches it can occupy.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Heijden |first1=E. W. Van der |last2=Kuyper |first2=Th W. |date=2001-01-01 |title=Laboratory experiments imply the conditionality of mycorrhizal benefits for ''Salix repens'': role of pH and nitrogen to phosphorus ratios |journal=Plant and Soil |language=en |volume=228 |issue=2 |pages=275–290 |doi=10.1023/A:1004850423794 |bibcode=2001PlSoi.228..275V |s2cid=22296398 |issn=0032-079X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=van der Heijden |first1=EW |last2=Vosatka |first2=M |date=2000-02-20 |title=Mycorrhizal associations of ''Salix repens'' L. communities in succession of dune ecosystems. II. Mycorrhizal dynamics and interactions of ectomycorrhizal and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi |journal=Canadian Journal of Botany |volume=77 |issue=12 |pages=1833–1841 |doi=10.1139/b99-178 |bibcode=2000CaJB...77.1833V |issn=0008-4026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Heijden |first=E. W. van der |date=2001-01-01 |title=Differential benefits of arbuscular mycorrhizal and ectomycorrhizal infection of ''Salix repens'' |journal=Mycorrhiza |language=en |volume=10 |issue=4 |pages=185–193 |doi=10.1007/s005720000077 |bibcode=2001Mycor..10..185V |s2cid=10605629 |issn=0940-6360}}</ref>

==Hybrids==
Creeping willow may hybridise with other ''Salix'' species, typically including goat willow (''[[Salix caprea|S. caprea]]'') and downy willow (''[[Salix lapponum|S. lapponum]]'').<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.luontoportti.com/suomi/en/puut/creeping-willow |title=Creeping Willow, ''Salix repens'' - Trees and shrubs - NatureGate |website=www.luontoportti.com |language=en |access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref> One especially rare hybrid (''S.'' × ''angusensis'') was discovered on Ainsdale Nature Reserve, [[Lancashire]] in 1993. It is a hybrid between three ''Salix'' species: ''S. cinerea'' ssp. ''oleifolia'' × ''S. repens'' var. ''argentea'' × ''S. viminalis''.<ref name="Bsbi">{{cite journal |last1=Meikle |first1=R.D. |last2=Robinson |first2=N.D. |title=A new record for ''Salix'' × ''angusensis'' (Salicaceae) Rech. f. from Ainsdale Sand Dunes National Nature Reserve, S. Lancs. v.c. 59 |journal=Watsonia |date=2000 |volume=23 |pages=327–330}}</ref>
